Strategic Report - continued
At the year end 99.3% (2024: 96.6%) of the gross loan boók was secured mortgage assets or senior securitisation positions. As a result of
the further growth in secured lending, the overall provision coverage has reduced to O.4% of gross loans held at amortisęd cost (2024:
1.6%), versus a coverage ratio of 36.84% (2024: 45.3%) against unsecured assets held at amortised cost.
Whilst the proportion of unsecured assets on its balance sheet is significantly smaller, the Group nonetheless recognises that despite the
decrease in the overall provision coverage, the risks to the performance of the unsecured book have remained heightened. This is a key
driver of the £1.7m impairment loșs in the Consolidated Statement of Total Comprehensive Income (2024: £O.9m).
On the liabilities side, customer deposits increased to £3,812m (2024: £2,857m), with the bank benefiting in particular from its newly
launched Easy Access product. It has managed to maintain an attractive cost of funds throughout the period, despite banking funding
costs rising more generally across the market.
The Group's funding capability has also benefitted from the approval by the Bank of England of Chetwood's inaugural securitisation as

the year, supplementing the bank's retail savings proposition.
The growth in the balance sheet and significantly improved revenue performance was offset to some extent by the continued significant
investment in the Group's underlying banking infrastructure and lending capabilities. Nonetheless, the Group still saw a reduction in its
loss after tax for the year to £4.7m (2024: £8.9m).
The continued significant investment during the financial year has focused predominantly on three particular areas; firstly in the building
its organic mortgage lending business, Moda Mortgages, which launched in July 2024, had contributed £12.6mi to the gross loan book by
year end and is now providing the business with a route to generate significant volumes of high quality organic BTL mortgages, as well as
the subsequent ability to innovate into other ancillary secured asset classes in time.
Secondly, the business has focused on the development of a more substantial retail deposit offering, which will enable Chetwood to
organically originate deposit volumes across the Easy Access and short-term fixed savings markets. Finally, the business has invested in
transitioning from internally built software (in particular via its Yobota banking platform) to more generic third party software. This latter
change is seen as vital to ensuring that Chetwood is able to deliver a streamlined and efficient cost base, and with lower contingent risk
in the maintenance and development of the firm's tech estate.

wholesale funding capability, and when combined the significant investment in organic mortgage and retail savings capabilities, has
nonetheless enabled the Group to progress significantly towards its goal of growing sustainably and reaching profitability in the coming

The Group is fortunate to have had the continuing support of its shareholders during this period, as well as the commitment of dedicated

Future developments
The principal investor has demonstrated their continued support of the Group's growth plans by injecting £27m of capital during the year
and a further £2Om between the balance sheet date and the date of signing. Further capital injections are anticipated in the coming year,
to support growth predictions.

The Group recognises the risks to business performance associated with the current macroeconomic uncertainty, and that the impact

The Group presents realised and unrealised gains and losses on loans and advances held at fair value in net income from financial
instruments held at fair value through profit and loss per Note 6. Within settlements / repayments is the write off of irrecoverable loans.
Loans and advances are valued using a discounted cash flow methodology, the significant unobservable inputs to the model are the
probability of default, loss given default, expected prepayment rates and the market discount rate. Significant increases in any of these
inputs in isolation would result in lower fair values. Expected prepayment rates are derived from historical prepayment trends,
probabilities of default and loss given default are derived from historical default and recovery information and adjusted for current
conditions.
36.8 Unconsolidated structured entities
Cherub Funding Limited ('Cherub') is a structured securitisation entity which the Group has previously contracted with the sale and
purchase of loans. Cherub is not consolidated by the Group as the Group does not control this entity and has minimal exposure to any
risks and rewards. The Group does not own any of the share capital or loan notes of this entity, nor does the Group have any entitlement
to any excess returns. The Group has no contractual arrangements with Cherub other than servicing the entity's loan portfolio. The Group
has not provided any financial support to Cherub and has no obligation or intention to do so. The maximum exposure to loss from the
unconsolidated structured entity is £nil (2024: £62k), being the servicing fee due from Cherub at the year end. On 20 Feb 2025, a special
resolution was passed to liquidate Cherub Funding Limited.
See note 38 for details of transactions with Cherub.
37 Capital management
The Company is subject to supervision by the PRA as an authorised bank. -The amount of capital held is measured against the regulatory
framework defined by the Capital Requirements Regulation ('CRR'). The Board manages capital levels for both current and future activities,
models stress scenarios and documents its risk appetite as part of the Internal Capital Adequacy Assessment Process (ICAAP). Chetwood
has previously been granted a solo-consolidation waiver by the PRA, allowing Chetwood to incorporate subsidiaries in the calculation of
its capital requirement under CRR Article 6(1). The regulatory capital requirements are therefore shown at a Group level only.

During the previous year, Chetwood undertook a fully retained securitisation of mortgage assets, with a carrying value of £1,120.8m. The
beneficial title of the assets was legally sold into a securitisation company, Chetwood Funding Limited 2024-1 ('CFL 2024-1'), however

on a company and consolidated basis. Chetwood accounts for the securitisation net, reducing the deemed loan balance by the principal
of the A and Z loan notes due.
Chetwood retains the risk and reward of the mortgages underlying the deemed loan and remits all collections on these mortgages to CFL
